newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks driven by bank alliance news.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks driven by bank alliance news.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed after a session driven by Thursday's announcement that Spain's Banco Central Hispano (BCH) would buy in to Colombia's second largest bank, Banco de Colombia.

Bogota's IBB index ended up 1.22 percent at 883.54 on a two billion peso volume, while Medellin's IBOMED general price index drifted down 0.03 percent to 13,630.33 on an 800 million peso trading volume.
Trading in Banco de Colombia was suspended after prices were artificially inflated by a wave of speculative buying on news that BCH could buy up as much as 36 percent of the bank.
"The market was driven by a lot of speculation of the announcement and the share had to be suspended between 10 a.m. and 11 a.m. The announcement took us all by surprise," one Bogota broker said.

Statements released in both Madrid and Bogota announced BCH's "strategic partnership" under which the Spanish bank will take between 26 percent and 36 percent of Banco de Colombia. The initial value of the operation is put at between $200 million and $260 million and will be achieved by an increase in share capital. Banco de Colombia ended its hectic session 10.57 percent up at 460 on a 597.7 million peso trade.
Dealing in the share was suspended as it hit 456 pesos. The broker said the prospect of a bigger rise was reined in by the suspension of trading and by a downward speculative wave.

"There's a lot of expectation about the way in which BCH will buy into Banco de Colombia, since it seems it will follow a similar route to that used by Banco Bilbao-Vizcaya, which bought some of its shares in Banco Ganadero (Colombia's largest bank) on the secondary market," the broker explained.
Banco de Colombia rose 8.36 percent to 447 on a 178.1 million peso trade.
"There was unsatisfied demand for Cementos Diamante -- shareholders were loath to sell and they only did so when they saw the price peaking," a Medellin broker said.

The IBOMED index was pushed down partly on the wave of profit-taking in Bavaria, which dropped 0.51 percent to 4,079 on an 8.4 million peso trading volume. It was also hit by a 0.28 percent drop in Banco Industrial de Colombia, down to 3,500 on a 43.9 million peso trade and a fall in cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco, down 3.84 percent to 3,000.01 on a 93 million peso trade.
